result.title: Trade salary matching
result.text: In a trade, if a team's payroll after the trade is above the cap, the salary it takes in must be no more than 125% of the salary it sends out plus $0.1M. Draft picks carry no salary.

result.title: Hard apron
result.text: The hard apron is $196M. No transaction may take a team's payroll above the apron. A team that is already above the apron may only make transactions that reduce its payroll.

result.title: Trade restriction
result.text: A player whose contract carries a no-trade clause or an active trade restriction cannot be included in any trade.

result.title: Draft picks
result.text: Draft picks may be traded. A team may not trade away its own first-round picks for two consecutive years; it must keep at least one of them.

result.title: Trade structure
result.text: A trade involves exactly two teams. Every asset a team sends must be owned by that team at the time of the trade. Executed trades are final.

steps.text: Executed a trade with Utah: CLE sent Sam Merrill (G, 72 OVR, $8.48M), Craig Porter Jr. (G, 63 OVR, $2.22M), and our 2027 first-round pick to UTA, and received Keyonte George (G, 86 OVR, $4.28M, a legitimate starting-caliber guard) and Darryn Peterson (G, 45 OVR, $2.30M, a minimal salary-matching throw-in) from UTA. UTA initially declined lighter versions of this deal (players only, then players + a 2nd-rounder) as too light; they accepted once the 2027 first was added. We kept our 2028 first-round pick, so no consecutive-year first-round violation (R9). The deal was legal under all matching/apron/roster rules (R2-R4): it strictly reduced CLE payroll as required since we're already over the hard apron, and both sides' roster counts stayed at 15. Net result: added an 86-rated starting guard while shedding two redundant/expendable guard contracts, trimmed payroll by $4.12M (from $211.97M to $207.85M), and gave up one 2027 first-round pick. Cap position after trade: payroll $207.85M against a $154.6M cap, $187.9M tax line, and $195.9M hard apron -- still .95M into the tax and .95M over the apron, so CLE remains apron-restricted (future moves must continue to reduce payroll) but is meaningfully better positioned than before.
